examples.en: That makes no sense.
He has an excellent sense of humor.
We had a long conversation.
This is a private conversation.
Can I ask one question?
Mom set the table for dinner.

note: поставити сто - to set the table

examples.en: Wait a second!
The race lasted ten seconds.
Turn around so I can look at you.

examples.sr: [О̀кренуо] сам број, али се нико не јавља.
examples.en: I dialed the number, but nobody answers.
My grandfather was a soldier.
The soldiers guarded the bridge.
The Serbian people love music.
A lot of people came to the concert.
Behave politely!
Why are you behaving like that?

meanings: to hurt, to ache (a body part)

examples.en: My head hurts.
Where does it hurt?

note: the person is in acc.: боли ме глава - my head hurts
tips: The 3rd person plural is «боле», not «болу»: «боли ме, боле ме ноге». «Болу» sounds childish.
«Боли ме глава/нога/леђа/грло/стомак»; «Боли ме уво за њих» - I couldn't care less about them.

forms: сетим се, сете се; impf. сећати се

examples.sr: Не могу да се [се̏тим] његовог имена.
examples.en: I can't remember his name.
I remembered that I had a meeting.

note: + gen.: сетити се нечега
tips: The perfective verb means remembering at a particular moment («сетио сам се њеног имена»). Its imperfective pair «сећати се» means to remember in general («сећам се детињства»).
To remember someone or something takes the genitive without a preposition: сетила сам се лепих тренутака. «Подсетити некога на + acc.» means to remind: подсети ме на договор.

examples.en: This costs two thousand dinars.
Thank you a thousand times!
The car is in excellent condition.
His condition is stable.

note: бити у стању - to be able to

examples.en: That's not important now.
This is an important decision for us.
The boss is in his office.
Our office is in the city center.
You promised you would come!
Promise me you'll be careful.
The banking system has crashed.
We have to change the way we work.
Thank you for your attention.
Pay attention to the signs.

related.en: to watch out, to look after

examples.en: People don't talk about sex in front of children.

examples.sr: У филму има превише [се̏кса] и насиља.
examples.en: There is too much sex and violence in the film.
He got into serious trouble.
A friend in need is a friend indeed.
Don't take my things without asking.
I take my medication twice a day.
Have you read that book?
Read the contract carefully.
I felt a sharp pain in my back.

examples.sr: [О̀сетила] сам да нешто није у реду.
examples.en: I sensed that something was wrong.
I've been learning Serbian for a year.
Mom taught me how to cook.

note: учити means both to learn and to teach
tips: A broad verb: to learn something, to teach someone (учим странце српском), to study. For years of schooling use школовати се, for university studies - студирати.
Prefixes: научити - to learn thoroughly, подучити - to teach a little, изучити - to study in depth, обучити - to train in a skill, учити се - to learn something by effort («учим се стрпљењу»).
No «се» is needed to say «I'm learning»: Учим српски.

forms: удам се, удају се; impf. удавати се

examples.en: My sister got married last year.
She wants to marry him.

note: of a woman: удати се за + acc.; of a man - оженити се
tips: The state of being married: «удата» (a woman only), «ожењен» (a man only): «она је удата», «он је ожењен».
To marry someone: за + acc.: «Удала сам се за Милоша». The state: «удата сам», «у браку сам».

examples.en: He's a bit strange.
At night we heard a strange sound.
I drink tea instead of coffee.
You go instead of me.

forms: сретнем, сретну; past срео; impf. сретати

examples.en: I ran into him in town by chance.

examples.sr: Драго ми је што смо се [сре̏ли].
examples.en: I'm glad we met.

examples.sr: Можеш ли да ми учиниш једну [у̏слугу]?
examples.en: Can you do me a favor?
The service in this restaurant is excellent.

tips: «Услужно» does not mean free of charge, but offered as a (paid) service: услужно печење - they roast the meat or fish you bought, услужно пеглање веша - ironing laundry as a service. «Самоуслужна» means self-service.

examples.en: The sky is full of stars tonight.
She is a big movie star.
That's a good sign.
Give me a sign when you're ready.
There, everything is done.
See, I wasn't lying.

note: ево - here (near me), ето - there (near you), ено - over there
tips: «Ето» is not only «there»: it also means «well, I told you so» («Ето видиш...») and a hesitant «well»: «- Како си? - Ето, добро.» «Ево» is used when handing something over, «ето» when it is near the listener, «ено» when it is far away.

examples.en: His work is highly valued.
I'm writing a term paper on history.

note: рад (adj.) means glad: рад сам да помогнем

meanings: to take care of, to see to
forms: побринем се, побрину се; impf. бринути се

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll take care of everything.
Who will take care of the dog?

note: побринути се за + acc. - to take care of someone or something

forms: поједем, поједу; past појео; impf. јести

examples.en: Who ate my chocolate?
Eat everything on your plate.
That was a difficult decision.
I've made the final decision.

note: донети одлуку - to make a decision

forms: родим, роде; part. рођен; impf. рађати

examples.en: I was born in Novi Sad.
She gave birth to a healthy baby girl.

note: «рођен сам» - I was born

examples.en: I often go for a walk along the river.
How often do you work out?
The sun is very hot today.
We sat in the sun all afternoon.
It's a pity you didn't come.
The storm did a lot of damage.

note: «Штета!» - What a pity!

examples.en: The kitchen is completely clean now.
I need a bit of fresh air.
My daughter loves animals.
What's your favorite animal?
Where is the bus stop?
They took him to the police station.
You've finally arrived!
The question has been settled once and for all.
This cake is too sweet.
What a cute puppy!

tips: Of a person or a child it means cute, adorable: «какво слатко дете».

examples.en: My brother is in the army.
The army entered the city.
I think it's a mistake.
Everyone considers him a hero.
He admitted that he had lied.
Admit that you like her!
We stayed at a hotel near the beach.
I booked a hotel for the weekend.
I usually get up at seven.
What do you usually do on weekends?
I won't say anything without a lawyer.
My lawyer will call you.
We lit a fire on the beach.
Don't play with fire!
Oh, you scared me!

examples.sr: Немој да се [у̀плашиш], то је само пас.
examples.en: Don't be scared, it's just a dog.
Do you speak English?
I love English literature.

note: говорити енглески - to speak English

examples.sr: [Већѝна] људи ради од девет до пет.
examples.en: Most people work from nine to five.
In most cases that's true.
Hang the picture on the wall.
This wall needs to be whitewashed.
I'm staying home tonight.
How long are you staying in Belgrade?
Nobody knows what the future will bring.
In the future I'll be more careful.
You're late again!
The train is half an hour late.
This is your home now.
I live in a student dormitory.

note: a building is usually кућа; дом здравља - health center
tips: «Дом» is the place where a person lives and feels at home (Овде ми је дом). A building is called «кућа». Also «Дом здравља» - a health center.

examples.en: I bought her a gift for her birthday.
Thank you for the gift!

tips: It can also mean a bow: «поклонити се» - to bow. «Поклон-бон» is a gift voucher.

examples.en: That's an excellent idea!
He is an excellent student.
He was thrown out of the club.
Throw out that old junk.

tips: «Избацити» means to throw out garbage (смеће) or to expel someone from a club. Of an ATM: «избацио је картицу» (spat out the card) and «није ми избацио паре» (did not give me my money). Imperfective - избацивати.

examples.en: It's obvious that he's lying.
He obviously doesn't know what he's doing.

forms: нападнем, нападну; past напао; impf. нападати

examples.en: The dog attacked a child in the park.
We were attacked from an ambush.
I see it differently.
Everything is different now.
She put on a red dress.
The driver went through a red light.
I won't let anyone hurt you.
Allow me to introduce myself.
Sorry, I'm busy right now.
This seat is taken.
They've been married for twenty years.
Their marriage wasn't happy.
He has nothing to do with drugs.
The police found drugs in the car.
What is the price of this jacket?
Prices have gone up again.
We live in a new apartment building.
That building has twenty floors.
Are you taking any medicine?
This is the best remedy for a cold.

note: лекар - doctor

examples.en: They have a little girl.
The girl is playing in the yard.

tips: «Девојчица» is a little girl, usually a daughter: «Како је твоја девојчица?» asks about a child. A girlfriend is «девојка».

meanings: to hand over, to pass on

examples.en: Hand this letter to the director.
Never give up!

tips: With «се» it means to surrender (предати се непријатељу); without it, to hand over or hand in (предао је домаћи).

examples.en: Why don't you answer the phone?
Does five o'clock suit you?

note: одговара ми - it suits me
tips: Besides «to answer»: «одговарати некоме» (dat.) means to suit («термин ми одговара»); «одговарати за» + acc. - to be responsible for one's actions; «одговарати стварности» - to correspond to reality.
It also means to bear responsibility («одговарам за своје дете») and to fit in size or convenience («не одговара ми овај прслук», «одговара ми термин»).
In a shop: «Одговара ми величина» - the size fits me; «Не одговара ми величина» - it does not; «Да ли имате већи/мањи број?» - do you have a bigger/smaller size?; «другу боју?» - another color?

examples.en: This stays between us.
He sat among friends.
He succeeded on the first attempt.
This is my last attempt.

tips: An attempt on someone's life is «атентат» («покушај убиства» also works).

examples.en: Smile for the camera!
The cameras filmed the thief.

forms: gen. прста; pl. прсти; gen. pl. прстију

examples.en: I cut my finger with a knife.
Don't point your finger at people!

tips: Names of the fingers: палац - thumb, кажипрст - index finger, средњи прст - middle finger, домали прст - ring finger, мали прст - little finger. On the foot, the second toe is «други прст» or «прст до палца».

examples.en: I bet he'll be late again.

examples.sr: Колико си се [кла̏дио] на ту утакмицу?
examples.en: How much did you bet on that match?
On Fridays we usually eat fish.
My dad likes to go fishing.

note: slang: риба - an attractive girl
tips: In youth slang «риба» is also a girl, usually an attractive one. Be careful: the tone can sound rude.
In youth slang «рибе» means girls: «гледају га рибе» - the girls are checking him out (not fish!).
Slang: «риба, рибица, рибетина» - a girl (not necessarily a beauty). Of a real beauty: «риба је као авион» - she's a stunner.

examples.en: See you in court!
Who will wash the dishes?

note: судови means both courts and dishes

examples.sr: Данас не идем на посао, [бо̏лестан] сам.
examples.en: I'm not going to work today, I'm sick.
She takes care of her sick mother.
We went to a club last night.
I support a football club from Belgrade.
Don't be an idiot!
I behaved like an idiot.
I promise I'll come back.

examples.sr: Он стално [обѐћава], а ништа не уради.
examples.en: He keeps promising, but never does anything.
I got up very early this morning.
I saw him in the shop this morning.

note: a single word meaning this morning

examples.en: I will love you forever.
He left forever.
Smoking kills.
This heat is killing me.
I'll pick you up in front of the building at eight.
Pick your things up off the floor.

tips: «Покупити дете из вртића» - to pick up a child from kindergarten. «Покупити нешто» - to pick something up.

examples.en: This is a serious problem.
Are you serious?
I barely made the train.
I can't wait for the weekend!

note: једва чекам - I can't wait

examples.en: What's your favorite color?
We bought paint for the walls.

tips: «Добити боју» - to get a tan: «Добила си боју!» - you got a tan. A tan (complexion) is «тен», to tan - «препланути», «поцрнети».
«У боји» means in color: фотографија у боји, штампач у боји. The adjective «обојен» means only dyed or painted, not «in color».

meanings: to use, to make use of

examples.en: Take advantage of this opportunity!
He just used you.
Two men are waiting outside.
I saw two men in front of the building.

note: двојица - for men; двоје - for a mixed group
tips: For groups of only men: двојица, тројица, четворица. For children and mixed groups: двоје, троје, четворо, петоро. For only women, ordinary numbers: две девојке.

examples.en: I'm dying of hunger!
The plant is dying without water.
The dog faithfully waits for its master.
He is the master of his fate.
My brother is very tall.
Prices here are too high.
I feel a sharp pain in my chest.
This pill will ease the pain.
Open the window, it's hot.
He looked out the window.
Excuse me, miss, is this yours?
Miss Petrović is our new teacher.
That little guy is a real devil.
Go to the devil!
The operation went well.
He has knee surgery tomorrow.
That's just plain stupidity.
Don't talk nonsense!
He is not my enemy.
The enemy attacked at night.
All the passengers survived the accident.
I won't survive another day like this.
My back aches from sitting.

examples.sr: Лежао је на [лѐђима] и гледао у небо.
examples.en: He lay on his back looking at the sky.

note: plural only: леђа ме боле
tips: «Леђа» - the back (plural): «Боле ме леђа» - my back hurts. The spine is «кичма»: «зеза ме кичма» - my spine is giving me trouble.
A plural-only word, so the verb is plural too: «боле ме леђа» (my back hurts), not «боли». Like наочаре, панталоне.

examples.en: Pack warm clothes for the weekend.
I usually buy clothes at the sales.
Why are you crying?
The baby cried all night.
This is especially important.
We'll pay separately, if that's possible.
Did you notice anything strange?
Nobody noticed that I had left.
I'll definitely come to your birthday party.
Can you help me? - Of course!
I spent the rest of the day in bed.
Finish the rest of the pizza.
You look tired today.

examples.sr: Лек почиње да [дѐлује] после пола сата.
examples.en: The medicine starts working after half an hour.
He neither drinks nor smokes.

examples.sr: Нисам га видео, [ни̏ти] сам чуо за њега.
examples.en: I haven't seen him, nor have I heard of him.

note: нити... нити - neither... nor
tips: It joins negations: Не зовеш ме нити се дружиш са мном (you neither call me nor hang out with me). The double form: Нити је био Аустријанац, нити је одрастао у Бечу (he was neither Austrian nor did he grow up in Vienna).
«Нити... нити...» means neither... nor...: «нити пијем, нити пушим». The verb takes no extra «не».

examples.en: What are you planning for the weekend?

examples.sr: [Пла̀нирамо] да се преселимо у Нови Сад.
examples.en: We're planning to move to Novi Sad.
I have an English class at five.
Wait, I'll be back in a moment.

note: час - lesson, moment; an hour is «сат»
tips: «Час» means a lesson («даје часове»), but also a moment: «у згодан час» - at the right time, «за час» - in no time, «у последњем часу» - at the last moment. The conjunction «час... час» means now... now....
«Претчас» is a zero period before classes begin.

examples.en: Everything went perfectly.
He speaks Serbian perfectly.
She is my best friend.
I went into town with a friend.

examples.sr: Нико те не може [на̀терати] да то урадиш.
examples.en: Nobody can make you do that.

examples.sr: [На̀терао] ме је да чекам сат времена.
examples.en: He made me wait for an hour.
One cold beer, please.
Shall we go for a beer after work?
Tell me what happened.
He told us a funny story.
What kind of music do you like?
I listen to music while I work.
It was terribly cold.
It's scary in the forest at night.

tips: In colloquial speech it is an intensifier meaning very: страшно висок, страшно ми се свиђа. So are ужасно, јако.

examples.en: Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
By the way, where are you from?

tips: Not only «otherwise»: a colloquial discourse word meaning «by the way, in general»: «Како сте иначе?» - how are you, in general?, «Иначе, можемо попити пиво» - by the way, we could have a beer.
As an aside it means «actually, by the way»: «Иначе, он је из Ниша.» (By the way, he's from Niš.) Not to be mixed up with «иначе» meaning «or else».

examples.en: The train arrives at five.
I can't manage to do everything.

note: «Стижем!» - I'm coming!
tips: Also «to have time to»: «Не стижем све» - I can't get everything done, «Стижеш ли?» - can you make it? To arrive: стићи у град.

examples.en: I need to make a phone call.
I got all my errands done this morning.
What's in that box?
I bought her a box of chocolates.
It was a lot of fun last night.
What's so funny about that?
The police freed the hostages.
Try to get rid of stress.

forms: оженим се, ожене се; impf. женити се

examples.en: My brother got married last summer.
Do you want to marry her?

note: of a man: оженити се + instr.; of a woman - удати се
tips: To marry someone takes the instrumental: «Оженио сам се Јеленом». The common mistake «оженио сам Јелену» means «I got Jelena married (to someone)», as in «кум је оженио сина» (the best man married off his son).

examples.en: It's an honor to meet you.
I give you my word of honor.

tips: «Част» means honor and respect, and also a treat (hospitality).

examples.en: Don't talk with your mouth full!
Open your mouth, please.

note: plural only: уста су
tips: «Уста» - the mouth, plural only (neuter): у устима, по устима. Not to be confused with «усне» (lips). Expressions about speech and eating: из уста у уста, на сва уста, вода на уста.
Plural in form, but it means one mouth: «отвори уста». «Очи» - eyes (more literary than the plural of «око»).

examples.en: He is my business partner.
He lives with his partner in Belgrade.
What's for lunch?

examples.sr: Позвали су нас на [ру́чак] у недељу.
examples.en: They invited us to lunch on Sunday.
He didn't commit that crime.
The crime scene has been cordoned off.

meanings: to get up, to stand up

examples.en: Get up, you're late for school!
I got up at five this morning.

examples.sr: Бог је [ство̏рио] свет за шест дана.
examples.en: God created the world in six days.
We've created an excellent team.
Who's paying for dinner?
I pay rent every month.
This is already his third book.

examples.sr: Ово ти је [тре̏ћӣ] пут да касниш.
examples.en: This is the third time you're late.
She hired a private detective.
The detective examined the crime scene.
That's my ex-boyfriend.
I met my ex-wife on the street.
I completely forgot about the meeting.
That's perfectly normal.

forms: повучем, повуку; past повукао; impf. повлачити

examples.en: Pull the door, don't push!
The army withdrew from the city.
People don't change.
Where can I exchange money?
I work at the seaside during the summer.
He called you during the meeting.
She wore a long white dress.
A glass of white wine, please.

note: m. бео, but f. бела: бео хлеб, бела кућа

forms: обучем, обуку; past обукао; impf. облачити

examples.en: Put on a jacket, it's cold.
She got dressed quickly and went out.

tips: «Обући» means to put on clothes or to dress a child: обучем, обуче, обуку (they); обукао сам дукс; «обући се» - to get dressed. For shoes use «обути».
One verb covers both putting on and dressing: обуци капут! (put on a coat), обукао сам, обући се - to get dressed. For shoes: обути: обуј ципеле! (past обуо сам).

examples.en: We once lived in Niš.
Sometimes I miss my old job.
Nobody is perfect.
This is a perfect day for the beach.
On weekends we go to Grandma's.
My grandma makes the best cakes.

tips: «Бака» is affectionate, «баба» neutral, «бабетина» disrespectful.

examples.en: I need a little rest.
Where are you going on vacation this year?

tips: Годишњи одмор - annual leave; распуст - school holidays; «лепо се проведите!» and «уживајте на одмору!» - wishes to someone on vacation.
At school: «велики одмор» - the long break (30 minutes), «мали одмор» - a short one, 5 minutes.

examples.en: The kids are playing in the yard.
I was still a kid then.

note: colloq.
tips: «Клинац» is a little guy, a kid. Sometimes used sarcastically of young people (a naive kid with his head in the clouds). The plural «клинци» means children: «Где су вам клинци?» - where are your kids?

examples.en: The general issued an order.
His grandfather was a general.
I went to the doctor yesterday.
Where were you yesterday afternoon?
The government passed a new law.
People are protesting against the government.
Honestly, I don't like it.
Tell me honestly what you think.
I get loads of messages every day.

examples.sr: Наш тим увек [добѝја] на домаћем терену.
examples.en: Our team always wins at home.
I'm not at home at the moment.
The medicine works almost instantly.

tips: At the moment, currently: «тренутно радим на пројекту». Not the same as «привремено» - temporarily.

examples.en: This house belongs to my father.
I feel that I belong here.
Farewell, we won't see each other again.
She said goodbye to him at the station.

note: a solemn farewell; everyday «bye»: ћао, здраво
tips: A serious, solemn farewell; in everyday life people more often say «довиђења» or «ћао».
Farewell with a sense of forever or solemnity. In daily life people say: довиђења, ћао, пријатно.

examples.en: I study French at school.
I like French cheese.
Where did you set off to?
I don't know where to go.

note: in speech often «где» instead: Где идеш?
tips: «Куда» is the standard «where to»; in colloquial speech «где» is often used instead: Куда ћемо на ручак? / Где ћемо на ручак?

examples.en: I'm afraid of heights.
He was trembling with fear.

meanings: to concern, to have to do with

examples.en: That doesn't concern you.

examples.sr: Што се мене [ти̏че], можеш да идеш.
examples.en: As far as I'm concerned, you can go.

note: што се тиче + gen. - as for, regarding
tips: Mostly used in the 3rd person: «тиче се» + gen.: «Ово се тиче свих» (this concerns everyone). «Што се тиче...» - as for..., «то ме се не тиче» - that doesn't concern me.

examples.en: We've been invited to a wedding.
The wedding is on Saturday in the church.

tips: In an invitation «венчање» can mean a church ceremony, a civil ceremony or the reception. Check the time and place in the invitation; «скуп сватова» - the gathering of the wedding guests.

examples.en: The baby has started to walk.
I like walking in the rain.

note: ходати - to walk; «to go somewhere» is ићи

examples.en: The room has a view of the sea.
At first glance he seemed decent.
You have a hole in your sock.
There's a big pothole in the road.

tips: «Рупа од стана» - a tiny, shabby flat: a hole rather than a home. «Мишја рупа» - a mouse hole.

examples.en: The police arrested the thief.
Arrest that man!
Can you prove it?
He proved that he was not guilty.
I live in the very center of the city.
Are we going downtown tonight?
Enter your personal data.
This data is incorrect.

forms: dat. банци; pl. банке; gen. pl. банака

examples.en: My sister works at a bank.
I need to go to the bank.

note: dat./loc. банци: у банци - at the bank
tips: «Банка» is a bank: «ићи у банку». A glass jar is «тегла», a tin can - «конзерва».

examples.en: They have a huge house in the country.
That's a huge problem.
I'm watching the film with subtitles.
This translation isn't very good.
Today is a special day.
We have a separate room for guests.

tips: «Особе са посебним потребама» - people with special needs (with disabilities). «Посебно» also means separately or in particular: «посебно бих хтео да се захвалим» - I would especially like to thank.

examples.en: We have a very good relationship.
What is your relationship with your parents like?

tips: From the root «нос» (to carry): однос (relation), ношња (costume), понос (pride), пренос (broadcast), унос (input), износ (amount).

examples.en: Serbia is a small country.
The state pays for schools.
It's raining outside.
The kids keep falling off their bikes.

note: пада киша/снег - it's raining/snowing

meanings: to have a chat, to talk

examples.en: Can we talk in private?
Let's talk tomorrow.
She turned down his offer.

examples.sr: Ако ти понуде посао, немој да [о̀дбијеш].
examples.en: If they offer you a job, don't turn it down.

tips: Senses: to decline («одбио сам позив»), to reject («одбили су моју пријаву»), to deflect («голман је одбио лопту» - the goalkeeper deflected the ball), to refuse entry («одбили су му улаз»).

examples.en: On Sundays we go to church.
This church is five hundred years old.
Which line goes to the center?
Draw a line under the text.
He broke his leg skiing.
Don't break my heart.
Where is the women's restroom?
This store sells women's clothing.
Welcome to Serbia!
You're always welcome at our place.

note: agrees with the person: добродошао (m.), добродошла (f.), добродошли (pl.)
tips: Of things and ideas it means allowed, appreciated: «Кућни љубимци су добродошли» (pets are welcome), «Савети су добродошли» (advice is welcome). The reply to «Добро дошли!» is «Боље вас нашли!».

examples.en: Tonight we're watching an American movie.
He has American citizenship.
Happy birthday!
What do you want for your birthday?

note: written as one word
tips: «Славити рођендан» - to celebrate a birthday, «Колико година пуниш?» - how old are you turning?, «Које си годиште?» - what year were you born?, «Лепо се проведите!» - have a good time!

forms: шаљем, шаљу; past слао; pf. послати

examples.en: I'm sending you the address in a message.
Mom sends me packages every month.
Lunch is already on the table.
I reserved a table for two.

note: сто (gen. стола) - table; сто is also the number 100

examples.en: That's impossible!
It's impossible to find an apartment in the center.
The children are playing outside.
It's very cold outside.

note: напољу - location; напоље - direction (out)
tips: For «outdoors, in the open air» use напољу: Да седнемо напољу или унутра? (Shall we sit outside or inside?)
Not just «outside»: «Она је напољу» - a child is out of the house, somewhere outdoors, playing with friends. Learn it by situation.

forms: лежим, леже; cf. лећи (to lie down)

examples.en: I lay in bed all day.
The book is on the table.

tips: Besides «to lie» it means to fit (of clothes): «ова хаљина ти лепо лежи» (this dress fits you nicely). Often paired with «стајати».

examples.en: The main character in the film is a detective.
Who's that guy by the door?

tips: In colloquial speech «лик» is a guy, a type: «неки лик»; «ликуша» - a girl or woman (about someone unknown).
In youth slang «лик» is simply a guy, a dude: «Знаш ли оног лика?» - do you know that guy? A colloquial word, not to be mixed up with the literary sense of image, face.

forms: придружим се, придруже се; impf. придруживати се

examples.en: Do you want to join us?
He joined the army at eighteen.

note: + dat.: придружити се коме

examples.en: We have a math test tomorrow.
The pregnancy test is positive.
There's no need to apologize.
Everyone has their own needs.
None of them came.
I don't have a single free evening this week.
